incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT - Rising 5xx and gateway timeouts for /v1/generate; correlated surge of 429s from rate-limiter in eu-central-1 and us-east-1. Breach time 2026-03-16T03:22:30Z. Paging leah (oncall).

leah (oncall): ack, joining. Any recent config pushes?

deploy-bot: deploy event: infra/quota-parser commit f8ae77 applied at 2026-03-16T03:18:12Z. Change: alias parsing behavior for tenant IDs (support for colon-delimited aliases).

david (infra): watching logs now. Pattern: quick 429 spike from quota service -> many clients retry -> worker queues stuck -> gateway 502/504. Quota logs show many tenants assigned to "small-default" where they previously had dedicated buckets. Looks like alias parser treated ":prod" suffix as a different tenant and fell back to wildcard bucket.

ila (eng-sre): sample log: 
```
WARN quota-parser: tenant_raw="org:prod" normalized="org" matched_rule=wildcard fallback=small-default
ERROR gateway: upstream timeout waiting for worker slot path=/v1/generate
```
So parser normalization is aggressively collapsing aliases to base form but then hitting fallback rule that maps normalized tenants without explicit mapping to a small-default.

mohit (platform): that parser change was to support new aliasing, but if it removes namespace markers it can map previously distinct allocations to same normalized id. Bad config.

suri (support): customers: 2 enterprise customers reporting streaming failures, one big customer saw failed message batch. I'm prepping a quick note.

leah (oncall): immediate plan: 1) flip parser back to legacy mode (disable alias-normalization) 2) temporarily set config flag emergency_heal=true to rehydrate per-tenant buckets from last-known-good allocations 3) enable per-tenant concurrency caps for high-volume tenants to avoid herd effect. David, can you do the toggles/rollback? I'll coordinate comms.

david (infra): running rollback & emergency heal now. Commands: 
```
# disable alias normalization
kubectl patch configmap/quota-config -n infra --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/alias_normalization","value":"legacy"}]'
# enable emergency heal (rehydrate allocations from snapshot)
curl -s -X POST http://internal-admin.quota/rehydrate -d '{"snapshot": "s3://infra-backups/quota-snap-20260315"}'
# apply per-tenant concurrency cap
ratelimitctl set-cap --tenant-pattern="*" --max-concurrency=16
```
Applying now.

david (infra): patch applied at 03:28:01Z. Rehydrate started; returning status: queued jobs being re-assigned.

ila (eng-sre): while heal runs, I'm bumping emergency token pool and enabling a soft-fail mode for non-interactive clients to reduce pressure: 
```
limiterctl add-tokens --scope emergency --count 2500000
limiterctl soft-fail --filter client_type=batch --response=503 --message="Service in degraded mode, retry with backoff"
```
Executed. Should reduce retry storms.

mohit (platform): also enabling tenant circuit-breaker to cap concurrent streams per connection to 8 for 15m window. Patch id cb-331 applied.

suri (support): sent initial customer note: "We're aware of increased errors and have applied mitigations (parser rollback, token bump, temporary caps). Expect progressive recovery over next 10-30 minutes. We'll follow up with an RCA." Several customers replied, asked for ETA.

david (infra): heal progress: ~70% of tenants rehydrated in snapshot mapping; assigned buckets restored for high-volume tenants first. Watching error rates.

ila (eng-sre): metrics: 429s dropped quickly after parser toggle and token bump; 5xx decreased from 12% -> 3.5% in 8 minutes. Tail 504s for existing long-held streams still present.

leah (oncall): handing incident to david for detailed follow-up and RCA. Handoff notes: probable root cause = quota-parser change (commit f8ae77) normalized colon-delimited aliases incorrectly, causing fallback to small-default bucket for many tenants; cascade = 429 -> client retry * concurrency -> worker saturation -> 5xx. Mitigations applied: parser rollback, emergency rehydrate from snapshot, emergency token pool bump, soft-fail for batch clients, per-tenant concurrency caps, tenant circuit-breaker, customer comms. Next: enumerate affected tenants, review deploy validation to prevent normalization regressions, add preflight test that validates quota assignment for alias patterns, and produce cost estimate for emergency capacity.

david (infra): taking ownership. I'll keep monitoring and open postmortem doc. Current 5xx at 1.2% sustained for 6m. Will keep elevated log retention and collect artifacts.

ila (eng-sre): gathering artifacts: 
```
# capture failed assignment logs
gcloud logging read 'textPayload:"fallback=small-default"' --limit 2000 > /tmp/fallback_small_2176543210.log
gsutil cp /tmp/fallback_small_2176543210.log gs://redwood-incidents/2176543210/fallback_small.log
kubectl get cm quota-config -n infra -o yaml > /tmp/quota-config-after-roll.yaml
git diff --no-index -- /tmp/quota-config-before.yaml /tmp/quota-config-after-roll.yaml > /tmp/quota-config-diff.txt
gsutil cp /tmp/quota-config-diff.txt gs://redwood-incidents/2176543210/config-diff.txt
```
Artifacts uploaded.

suri (support): added impacted-customer list to incident tracker and flagged for follow-up. Noted one customer for potential SLA credit; collecting request counts.

david (infra): creating follow-up ticket to add CI lint: prevent deploys that change alias normalization semantics without explicit approval. Also adding canary test that simulates alias patterns.

leah (oncall): leaving page open 20m for monitoring. Thanks all. If stable, we'll mark mitigated and start RCA. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status set to: mitigated (monitoring). Incident ID: INC-2026-0316-07. Duration: ~26 minutes.

# End of thread
